City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 20, 2022
  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, September 20, 2022

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Menchaca
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Ding, Vice Mayor Harrington, Council Members Menchaca,
  Rivera, Wu

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS – None.

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. RESOLUTION NO. 22-57 REAUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL AND THE
  CITY’S COMMISSIONS TO IMPLEMENT TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY
  FOR CONDUCTING PUBLIC MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361

  Resolution No. 22-57 makes findings that allow the City to continue
  implementation of teleconference/internet-based accessibility for public
  meetings under state-of-emergency provisions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-57 regarding
  the use of teleconferencing for public meetings.

  B. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of September 6, 2022.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of September 6, 2022.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 20, 2022  2
   C. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  D. MONTHLY BUDGET UPDATE – AUGUST 2022

  This report provides the monthly budget update for the City’s General Fund
  and Mission Playhouse as of August 31, 2022. The monthly budget incorporates
  the actual revenue received and expenditures that have occurred through
  August 31, 2022, and projects the financial results for the year ending on June
  30, 2023. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report.

  E. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – AUGUST 2022

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2022-2023 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 22-30) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The August 2022 Cash and
  Investment Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s
  adopted 2022-2023 Investment Policy.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for August 2022.

  F. RENEWAL OF FACILITIES JOINT USE AGREEMENT WITH SAN GABRIEL
  UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT

  On April 6, 2021, the City Council approved the Amended and Restated
  Facilities Joint Use Agreement with the San Gabriel Unified School District. The

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 20, 2022  3
   term of the amended agreement was from May 1, 2017 to April 30, 2022, with
  the possibility of extension for an additional five (5) years upon mutual written
  consent by both parties. For hours of operation outside of regular
  school/custodial hours, the City pays for the custodian’s time.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve the proposed
  Amended and Restated Facilities Joint Use Agreement and authorize the City
  Manager and Mayor to execute the agreement.

  G. PURCHASE OF A CATERPILLAR MINI EXCAVATOR FOR THE WASTEWATER
  OPERATIONS DIVISION

  The Wastewater Operations Division has been utilizing rented mini excavators
  from multiple suppliers to complete several small stormwater infiltration
  projects. Purchasing a mini excavator with accessories and a trailer will allow
  staff to expand service, improve efficiency, reduce project costs, and shorten
  emergency response time. The total amount of the purchase for the Caterpillar
  brand Mini Excavator with the equipment trailer is $99,173.30, which is included
  in the adopted Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Budget in the Sewer fund.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive formal bidding and authorize the
  Cooperative Purchase Agreement consistent with the piggyback bidding requirements
  pursuant to Municipal Code Section 34.35; and authorize the City Manager to approve
  a Purchase Order with the Quinn Company in the amount not to exceed $99,173.30
  from budget account 124-800-38-66-405.

  H. AWARD  CONSTRUCTION  CONTRACT  NO.  22-05  TO  PALP,
  INCORPORATED DOING BUSINESS AS EXCEL PAVING COMPANY IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $4,866,957.50 FOR THE ANNUAL STREETS PROGRAM FISCAL
  YEAR 2022-2023

  As part of the City’s ongoing effort to consistently improve and preserve the
  quality of our roadways, the Public Works Department has created an annual
  streets program for Fiscal Year 2022-2023. A few streets and all of the alleys will
  get a full-width 4-inch thick grind, and then apply 1.5 inches of asphalt rubber
  hot mix (ARHM) over 2.5 inches of conventional asphalt concrete (AC). San
  Gabriel Boulevard between north city limit to Las Tunas Drive will get a full-
  width 2-inch thick grind, and then 2 inches application of an ARHM overlay.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 20, 2022  4
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve plans and specifications for the Annual Streets Program Fiscal Year
  2022-2023, Contract No. 22-05;
  2. Award the contract to Excel Paving Company as the lowest responsive and
  responsible bidder and authorize the City Manager to execute contract
  agreement for the total bid amount of $4,866,957.50; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with Excel Paving
  Company in the amount of $5,066,918, which includes a 4% construction
  contingency.

  I. ORDINANCE NO. 685 DELETING TITLE III, CHAPTER 32, SECTION 32.70
  FROM THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE TO REMOVE THE MISSION
  PLAYHOUSE DEPARTMENT

  The Mission Playhouse Department has been consolidated into the Community
  Services Department for budgeting and administrative purposes. This item
  begins the process of amending the City’s Municipal Code to formalize this
  change. There is no fiscal impact as Mission Playhouse budgeting has been
  consolidated in the Community Services Department as of the Fiscal Year 2021-
  2022 Adopted Budget.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive full reading, introduce by title
  only, and waive future reading of Ordinance No. 685, “An Ordinance of the City
  Council of San Gabriel, California, Deleting Title III, Chapter 32, Section 32.70 of
  the San Gabriel Municipal Code to Remove the Mission Playhouse
  Department,” and schedule the second reading and adoption of the Ordinance
  for the next regular City Council meeting.

  J. APPROVAL OF SAN GABRIEL MISSION PLAYHOUSE FAÇADE AND
  PORTICO RESTORATION IN THE AMOUNT OF $52,150 AND APPROVAL OF
  RESOLUTION NO. 22-58 AMENDING FISCAL YEAR 2022-2023 BUDGET TO
  RECEIVE GRANT FUNDS AND ALLOCATE FUNDS FOR THE PROJECT

  Over the past several years, the exterior portions of the Mission Playhouse have
  been undergoing a restoration process. The first phase of the project included
  painting the entire exterior of the building, with the exception of the decorative
  details. Phase II includes the decorative details, such as the façade crest and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 20, 2022  5
   moldings, the portico, lighting sconces and display cases. Donations of
  $2,166.46 and a grant of $3,500 were previously collected for this Phase II
  Façade Restoration Project.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Authorize the City Manager to execute an Agreement with LeGrande
  Studios, Incorporated subject to formal approval by the City Attorney;
  2. Accept the grant from National Trust for Historic Preservation for $3,500;
  accept the grant from The Ahmanson Foundation for $15,000; accept
  donations from individual donors totaling $14,796.96; and transfer the
  remaining amount of $18,853.04 from the Mission Playhouse fund to cover
  the cost of the Phase II Façade Restoration;
  3. Approve Resolution No. 22-58 amending the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 budget
  to reflect the changes to the City’s account; and
  4. Approve the expenditures totaling $52,150 to Evan Wilson of LeGrande
  Studios, Incorporated for the work for the Façade Restoration.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. DONATION OF ASSEMBLY BILL 481 MILITARY EQUIPMENT RESCUE
  VEHICLE

  The County of Los Angeles, Bureau of Investigations of the District Attorney’s
  Office recently notified Staff that their armored rescue vehicle was being
  relinquished for donation to a local Police Department. Staff is seeking approval
  to accept the donation due to the Police Department’s dire need of a rescue
  vehicle to conduct life-saving measures during critical incidents. By accepting
  the donation and transfer of the Ford armored rescue vehicle from the County
  of Los Angeles, the City will experience significant cost savings of approximately
  $400,000 since the vehicle is in excellent condition and does not require
  additional funding for immediate operational use. Assembly Bill 481 requires
  approval from City Council for all military equipment purchases and donations
  to comply with Government Code 7071.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 20, 2022  6
   Staff recommends City Council approve and provide the City Manager the
  authority to accept the donation of a 2008 Ford armored rescue vehicle from
  the County of Los Angeles, Bureau of Investigations from the District Attorney’s
  Office.

  B. DISCUSSION REGARDING THE INTERNAL PROSECUTION MISDEMEANOR
  AND OTHER QUALITY-OF-LIFE CRIMES

  On April 19, 2022, the City Council received a presentation and report from staff
  regarding alternatives for prosecuting local misdemeanor crimes. At the conclusion of
  that item, the City Council directed staff to return at a future meeting with further
  information and analysis regarding options for prosecution of quality-of-life crimes
  that negatively impact the community. Based upon further discussion with the District
  Attorney’s office and other cities that have been working through the local prosecution
  of misdemeanors, it appears as though creating local infractions in our municipal code
  is a more appropriate approach given the circumstances.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends City Council discuss the staff report and options for the local
  prosecution of misdemeanors and other quality-of-life crimes and provide direction to
  staff on how to proceed with this item.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

 12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, October 4, 2022 at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.
